That seems like something it's most natural to state purely as a number theory problem, without involving geometry at all (just like the classification of Pythagorean triples).

There are some geometrical number theory problems that have more geometrical content and so might more naturally be stated in terms of geometrical definitions. E.g. IMO 2016 problem 3, which we can't state at present because it involves areas and I don't think we have two-dimensional Lebesgue measure yet.

One question the IMO Grand Challenge will need to consider is how literal the formal versions should be of algebra / combinatorics / number theory problems expressed for humans in geometrical terms: should the formal version also be expressed geometrically so a formal solution needs to include the reduction to algebra / combinatorics / number theory, even if that reduction is both so trivial to humans that they wouldn't mention it in an informal solution, and possibly harder to formalize than the main substance of a solution?

@Reid Barton do you still have the code, by any chance?

Reviving a pretty old thread. This came up here about six years ago (the x⁴−y⁴=z² descent, and an early Lean version of it), and as far as I can tell it's still not in Mathlib. I've since worked out both forms and wanted to check interest and get a steer on naming and placement before opening anything.

The two statements, both over ℤ, stated purely as number theory with no geometry, going through the existing PythagoreanTriple classification (which matches the framing suggested earlier in this topic).

First, a⁴ − b⁴ = c² forces c = 0:

theorem eq_zero_of_pow_four_sub_pow_four_eq_sq (a b c : ℤ)
    (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) (h : a ^ 4 - b ^ 4 = c ^ 2) : c = 0

The naive a⁴ − b⁴ ≠ c² is false, since the trivial family with |a| = |b| and c = 0 satisfies it, so the honest content is that c = 0 is forced.

Second, and closely related, four squares can't form a nonconstant arithmetic progression (also Fermat):

theorem no_four_squares_in_ap (r s t u D : ℤ) (hD : D ≠ 0)
    (h1 : s ^ 2 = r ^ 2 + D) (h2 : t ^ 2 = s ^ 2 + D) (h3 : u ^ 2 = t ^ 2 + D) : False

A naming heads up on the second one. This is not Lagrange's four square theorem. Mathlib already has Nat.sum_four_squares in SumFourSquares.lean, which says every natural is a sum of four squares. This is about four squares in arithmetic progression, a different result, so I've kept "in AP" explicit in the names.

The nearest existing material is not_fermat_42 (a⁴ + b⁴ ≠ c²) in NumberTheory/FLT/Four.lean. Both of mine are separate infinite descents, each through PythagoreanTriple.coprime_classification', and the AP form also routes through Euler's concordant form (1,4). Neither is reachable from not_fermat_42 by a short identity, so they'd sit alongside the existing Fermat42 material rather than falling out of it.

On status, both compile against current Mathlib with Mathlib imports only, #lint is clean, and #print axioms gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], with no sorry and no native_decide.

To be upfront: these were developed with AI - my own experimental agentic system in my continued research to develop rigorous engineering systems. I hope that doesn't suck the fun out of it!

A few questions. Would these be welcome, and is anyone already working on either? On placement, I was leaning toward the minus form as a sibling file at NumberTheory/FLT/FourMinus.lean next to Four.lean, and the AP form in its own file. On naming, I'm happy to match whatever convention you prefer, whether a Fermat42 style namespace or a headline phrased with ¬ instead of ending in : False.

Thanks!
